groups.name: raw RNA-seq count matrix
groups.reason: counts.csv and metadata.csv share the local/<word>.csv naming template but are different substrates: one is the numeric expression matrix consumed as measurement data, the other is a small sample-annotation table consumed as design metadata to interpret the matrix's columns. A downstream step (e.g. differential expression) reads them through entirely different code paths.
groups.description: A 12000-gene x 12-sample table of raw (integer, unnormalized) RNA-seq counts. Gene identifiers are a mix of ~4384 real HGNC-style gene symbols (many from lipid/fatty-acid metabolism and adipocyte biology, e.g. ABCA1, ADIPOQ, ACOX1, ACADM, ACADL, ACLY) and ~7616 synthetic placeholder IDs (GENE00001-GENE07616) with no biological annotation. Sample columns sample_01..sample_12 correspond 1:1 to the rows of the metadata sheet.
groups.memberRepresents: the complete gene x sample raw read-count matrix for the bulk RNA-seq experiment (all 12 samples, one row per gene)

memberAnnotations.note: Confirmed via full-file scan: 12000 gene rows, all count values are non-negative integers (raw counts, not normalized). Gene ID column mixes real gene symbols (first ~4384 rows, thematically clustered around lipid/fatty-acid oxidation and adipocyte genes) with placeholder IDs GENE00001-GENE07616 (remaining ~7616 rows) - consistent with a simulated/benchmark dataset rather than a real annotated transcriptome.

groups.description: Two-column sample sheet (sample, condition) mapping each of the 12 sample IDs to a two-arm design: sample_01-06 = control, sample_07-12 = treated. Balanced 6 vs 6.
groups.memberRepresents: the sample-to-arm assignment table used to interpret each count-matrix column

memberAnnotations.note: Read in full (13 lines): only columns are sample and condition; condition takes exactly two values, control (6 samples) and treated (6 samples), in perfect balance and matching the count matrix's 12 sample columns.

groups.name: gene length reference table
groups.description: A two-column (gene, length) lookup table covering exactly the same 12000 gene identifiers as the count matrix (1:1 match confirmed by set comparison), with lengths ranging ~236-18887 bp (median ~1999 bp). This is external reference data the analysis would consume - not produced by the experiment - typically used for length-based normalization (TPM/FPKM) or length-bias correction in downstream enrichment testing (e.g. goseq-style methods).
groups.memberRepresents: the canonical length in base pairs of one gene, keyed to the same gene identifier used in the count matrix

probes.reason: metadata.csv carries only sample and condition columns; there is no subject identifier distinct from sample and no repeated-measures structure - each of the 12 samples is treated as an independent biological replicate.
no visit/day/timepoint column or filename token; the design is a single-timepoint two-arm comparison.
no plate/lane/run/centre column or run-date token; metadata.csv records only sample and condition.

caveats: Organism is not stated anywhere in the inputs (no organism/species column, no README, no accession). The non-placeholder gene symbols follow human-style all-caps HGNC nomenclature (e.g. ABCA1, ADIPOQ) rather than mouse Title-case, but per policy this alone does not establish species - organism is recorded as unknown/null until confirmed by the user or another source.

~7616 of the 12000 genes (~63%) are synthetic placeholder IDs (GENE00001-GENE07616) carrying no real biological annotation; only ~4384 genes have real HGNC-style symbols, many clustered thematically around lipid/fatty-acid oxidation and adipocyte biology (ABCA1, ADIPOQ, ACOX1, ACADM, ACADL, ACLY, ACO2, ANGPTL4, etc.). This pattern is characteristic of a synthetic/simulated benchmark built to test differential expression + pathway-enrichment recovery of a planted metabolic signal against a large uninformative background - any gene-set enrichment step will only be able to map the non-placeholder subset to real pathway databases, and the placeholder genes should be expected to enter downstream results as unannotated background, not as evidence against the biological signal.
No README, paper, or accession was provided; every identity and design fact above comes solely from the three CSV files' own content.

Count matrix holds raw, unnormalized integer values (verified: no non-integer entries) - any differential-expression step must apply its own size-factor/library-size normalization; gene_lengths.csv is available if TPM/FPKM-style length normalization or length-bias correction (e.g. goseq) is wanted.
Design is perfectly balanced (6 control vs 6 treated) with no recorded batch, timepoint, or subject covariates - there is nothing to adjust for beyond the two-arm comparison itself.
result.summary: This is a small, self-contained bulk RNA-seq dataset built for a two-group differential-expression (and likely downstream enrichment) analysis: a 12000-gene x 12-sample raw count matrix (counts.csv), a 12-row sample sheet assigning each sample to a control or treated arm in a balanced 6-vs-6 design (metadata.csv), and a gene-length reference table covering the identical 12000 genes 1:1 (gene_lengths.csv), presumably for length-based normalization or enrichment bias correction. Organism is not stated by any input; gene symbols use human-style HGNC nomenclature but that alone does not establish species, so organism is left null. Roughly 63% of the genes in the matrix are synthetic placeholder IDs (GENE00001-GENE07616) rather than real annotated genes, while the remaining ~4384 real gene symbols skew toward lipid/fatty-acid metabolism and adipocyte biology - a pattern consistent with a simulated/benchmark dataset engineered to test recovery of a planted metabolic gene-set signal via DE + enrichment, rather than a dataset from a real sequencing experiment. No documentation, README, or public accession accompanies the files. The data supports a straightforward two-group DE analysis (e.g. control vs treated) but enrichment/pathway analysis will only be able to annotate the non-placeholder subset of genes, and the synthetic nature of the placeholder genes should be disclosed in any downstream report rather than treated as biological signal or noise.

dimensions.label: treatment arm (control vs treated)
dimensions.description: Two-arm design assigned by the experiment: 6 samples labeled control, 6 labeled treated (sample_01-06 vs sample_07-12). This is the primary comparison the count matrix supports.

dimensions.label: sample identity
dimensions.description: 12 sample IDs, each mapping 1:1 to one column of the count matrix. No subject or replicate hierarchy above the sample level was found.

result.experimentalDesign: Two-group (unpaired) bulk RNA-seq design: 6 control vs 6 treated samples, balanced, no subject/timepoint/batch structure recorded. Count matrix is 12000 genes x 12 samples of raw integer counts; a companion gene-length reference table covers the identical 12000-gene set 1:1, letting length-based normalization or enrichment bias correction be applied downstream. No replicate pairing or repeated measures - each sample is treated as one independent biological replicate.
